purpose: Exploratory analysis of whether role information in scene-tower states contributes causally to unseen-pair decisions after ordered-role training.
checkpoints: The first prespecified training start (271001) on each of the eight fresh confirmation graphs, ordered_roles and unordered_identities only: 16 existing frozen checkpoints.

probe.features: Scene tower CLS state after first block, second block, and final normalized output; no model weights changed.
probe.labels: Ordered source and target entity IDs (two 10-way readouts).
probe.fit_data: Observed pairs only: both directions and events, all eight legal distractors, scene seed 620107.
probe.test_data: All 25 unseen pairs: both directions and events, all eight legal distractors, independent scene seed 620108.
probe.method: Fixed ridge linear regression with lambda 0.1 on training-standardized features; no unseen-pair tuning.
probe.metric: Joint source-and-target exact decoding accuracy on unseen pairs, reported at all three states.

intervention.data: The second confirmation rendering (scene seed 260108), all 25 unseen pairs, 128 balanced episodes per pair (repeat index 0 from each direction/event/answer/distractor cell).
intervention.role_subspace: Top 18 singular vectors of the 20 source/target decoder weight columns fitted on observed scenes, mapped back to raw final-state coordinates. Each 10-way readout has one sum-to-zero dependency, so its informative rank is at most 9.
intervention.operation: Exchange only the role-subspace components of the correct and role-reversed candidate scene embeddings, keep the query and other candidates fixed, then renormalize the two changed embeddings.
intervention.controls: Five deterministic random 18-dimensional subspaces for each model and a full candidate-embedding swap positive control.
intervention.metrics: Correct-versus-reversed margin and binary role accuracy before and after each intervention; changes are paired within the same episodes.

analysis_unit: Graph means over one fixed seed; this stage is an exploratory mechanism diagnostic, not a fresh independent replication of the behavioral confirmation.
limits: A linear readout and projected-state swap show accessibility and causal contribution of a subspace, not unique localization or the complete computation. Scene source movement is a cue; the diagnostic does not establish natural-language or LLM mechanisms.
